question: Do personal release-zone huck tendencies persist into later seasons, beyond league geometry?

source.freshnessCaveat: Computation uses exported rows. Live season counts match; row contents were not refetched or proven identical.

method.primary: Train on 2021–2025 regular seasons, evaluate 2026 regular season.
method.chronologicalChecks: Expanding earlier history predicts 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 separately; folds overlap in training and players and are not independent experiments.
method.huck: Nonstall pass; receiver Y minus thrower Y strictly >30 AND Euclidean distance strictly >40 yards.
method.complete: Source turnover flag is false. Drops count as incomplete attempts.
method.identity: Source PlayerID/Thrower, with one name per ID; same-name distinct IDs are not merged.
method.bestZone: At least 40 prior hucks and at least two zones with 10 prior hucks. Choose highest raw completion, ties by attempts then zone ID. Compare against all other zones for same player. Raw selection is deliberately optimistic and is evaluated on a later season.
method.attemptChoice: Release Y 20 to <60 only. At least 40 past hucks in this depth window; at least two zones with 100 throws and 5 hucks for a preferred-zone selection. Outcome is hucks / all located nonstall passes.
method.prediction: Six regularized binomial models: league zone + geometry; player; player + shared zone; add player-zone interaction; player + shared zone + geometry; add interaction to geometry model. All fit on past years, with fixed penalties and no tuning on test outcomes. Main test cohort requires 40 past hucks; a sensitivity uses 10.
method.geometryCompletion: 10-yard flight-length and forward-gain categories, plus whether the endpoint is in the scoring end zone. Conditional on attempted throw; these endpoint features are not known before a throw and do not represent an actionable pre-throw forecast.
method.geometryAttempt: 10-yard release-depth categories, within Y20–60. Player + shared zone baseline already includes common left/center/right field tendencies.
method.uncertainty: 5,000 bootstrap resamples, seed 20261024. Loss differences resample entire test games and separately entire test players. Neither alone handles all crossed player/game/opponent dependence. Best-zone gaps resample players with equal player weight. Conditional on fitted historical models; no correction for multiple exploratory comparisons.
limitations: Historical observational associations, not causal effects of changing release location.
2026 previously inspected; exploratory temporal validation, not preregistered or external untouched testing.
No receiver movement at release, defensive pressure, marking, wind, stall count or throw technique.
Season and team context, roles and opponents can change. Stable source IDs may still split an individual if upstream IDs change.
No claim of truly best coaching strategy follows from completion alone; possession value and alternatives matter.
